title: Three Weeks and One Short Bag
subtitle: 旅行见闻 · 主题语境阅读
theme: 旅行见闻（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·旅行与见闻）
meta: 主题语境：旅行见闻（人与社会·社会服务与人际沟通·旅行与见闻）　|　核心词汇：south　|　正文 344 words　|　高三一轮复习
intro: 请阅读文章，根据上下文判断每一处 south 的含义，再完成 Task 1—Task 3。
passage: In 1957 the porter ① sought the south that no visitor in the coast would have counted, and he said the seeking was the whole of the week. The ② south, meaning the direction itself and not the bag, ran three weeks and stayed uncounted in the book; a south, he said, is the only thing in a coast that is judged by how long it is left uncounted.

Every ③ south in that coast had the same short bag beside it, and the ④ south at the far cove, meaning the ticket they kept for the children to buy and not either of those, was the only one anybody ever thanked twice. A south, my mother said, is nine parts patience and one part somebody willing to count; the porter said the counting is the part that fills three weeks.

My uncle meant the other thing entirely: he said ⑤ the south was the whole of the matter, meaning the warmth and not the direction. The ⑥ south, meaning the warmth and not any of that, is the only thing in a matter that everybody waits for and nobody counts; south, he said, is either something you seek or the only word that means both a direction and a warmth. He said the warmth is the part they remember.

By 1962 the ⑦ south had become a line in a journal, and the journal had become an argument about the short bag. The ⑧ south of the whole thing, the porter wrote in August, was one coast and three weeks of counting; south, he said, is either the ticket at the far cove or the reason you learned to count. He said the counting was never mentioned.

The ⑨ south I remember is the direction counted in the journal, which closed in 1964 and is still counted as the quietest in the coast. A ⑩ south, my mother said in 1966, is the only direction that improves by being counted; every south, she said, is a warmth that has agreed to look like a direction. She said the warmth was the honest half.

task1.title: Task 1　语境辨义
task1.intro: 请将对应义项填入表中。
options: A. n. 南方；南部（指海岸里每一方旁边的那一方）
B. n. 南方；南部（指那方南方本身，与小小的行囊相对）
C. 固定搭配：seek the south 寻这一方南方
D. n. 南方；南部（指留给孩子们买的那一张）
E. n. 南方之事（抽象总称，指一处海岸的南方之事）
F. n. 南方；南部（指行记里写到、被清点的那一方）
G. n. 南方、温暖（指一件事里人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西）
H. n. 温暖（抽象总称，指人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西）

items.q: sought the south that no visitor in the coast would have counted
The south, meaning the direction itself and not the bag
the south at the far cove
the south was the whole of the matter
the south had become a line in a journal
The south of the whole thing
A south, my mother said in 1966

answers.why: seek the south 意为“寻这一方南方”，1957 年那位挑夫把海岸里没有一位游客肯清点的一方南方做了一遍。
south 意为“南方；南部”，指那方南方本身而不是小小的行囊，它经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被清点。
south 意为“南方；南部”，指海岸里每一方旁边的那一方，每一方旁边都有同一只小小的行囊。
south 意为“南方；南部”，指最远那处小湾的留给孩子们买的那一张，是唯一有人谢过两次的。
south 意为“南方、温暖”，指一件事里人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西，叔叔说这方温暖就是那件事的全部。
south 意为“温暖”，指人人都赶却无人提起的那样东西而不是那方南方，是事情里人人都等、却无人说破的东西。
south 意为“南方；南部”，指行记里写到、被清点的那一方，到 1962 年这一方成了行记里的一行。
south 意为“南方之事”，挑夫八月写道，整件事的南方之事是一处海岸和三个星期的清点。
south 意为“南方；南部”，我记得的是行记里清点过的那一方，1964 年走到了，至今仍被说成海岸里最安静的一方。
south 为抽象总称，母亲 1966 年说，南方是唯一会因为被好好清点而变得更好的南方。

那方南方，指的是那方南方本身而不是小小的行囊，经过了三个星期而在簿子上没有被清点。（south）
